independent_solution: Fall: v = gt, so K = (1/2) m g^2 t^2 rises as a concave-up parabola. Contact: the restoring force ~ compression (spring-like), so the ball decelerates smoothly to rest at maximum compression (K = 0) and re-accelerates.
It returns to its original height, so K just after contact equals K just before; rising, K = (1/2) m (v0 - g t')^2 falls as a concave-up curve to 0.
In the sketches (pinned page 1): (A) is concave-down, (C) has no dip to zero, (D) is linear in t; only (B) shows concave-up rise, a dip to zero, and concave-up fall.

The wall exerts an impulse on the molecule (its normal component 200 cos30 reverses), so the molecule's own momentum changes; the wall gets the opposite change, so the momentum of molecule + wall is conserved.
Rebound at the same speed: the molecule's kinetic energy is unchanged (the massive wall takes none), so the collision is elastic.
questions.independent_answer: Yes, momentum of molecule + wall is conserved; elastic
questions.official_answer: Yes, momentum of the molecule + wall system is conserved. Since kinetic energy is also conserved, the collision is elastic.

independent_solution: (a) Impulse = change of momentum from rest: 0.5 kg x 25 m/s = 12.5 N s.
(b) Toward the wall positive: p_before = +0.5 x 25 = +12.5 kg m/s; p_after = -0.5 x 12.5 = -6.25 kg m/s; change = -18.75 kg m/s, i.e. 18.75 kg m/s away from the wall.
